access.title: Asana API Guide: Get Tasks, Projects, and Users in 2026
access.snippet:
Asana's API is a REST interface that speaks JSON at `https://app.asana.com/api/1.0`, and you can list tasks with a personal access token and a `GET /tasks` call, the same kind of call that tools like [Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com) make under the hood when they talk to Asana.

The official reference lives at [developer.asana.com](https://developer.asana.com/reference).

### Which Asana plans include API access
You create a personal access token from your own account's developer settings, and Asana's developer documentation describes the API as available to Asana accounts.
Plan details change over time. Confirm them on Asana's pricing page and the developer docs before you build a dependency on a particular tier. To check access, make a single `GET /users/me` call with your token.

| | Personal access token | OAuth app | Service account |
|---|---|---|---|
| Who it acts as | The user who created it | Each user who authorizes the app | A dedicated non-human user, where your Asana plan offers one |
| Best for | Your own scripts and one-off pulls | Products used by other people | Unattended jobs that should outlive any one employee |
| How it's sent | `Authorization: Bearer <token>` | `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` | `Authorization: Bearer <token>` |
| Scopes behaviour | Carries the full access of its owner | Limited to the scopes the user approves | Limited to what that account can see |
| Setup effort | Minutes, from the developer console | Registration, redirect URI, consent flow, token refresh | Account provisioning, then a token like any other |

You pay for every page in requests. Asana caps them at 1,500 per minute on a paid domain, 150 on a free domain and 60 for the Search API, according to [Asana's rate-limits page](https://developers.asana.com/docs/rate-limits).

At 150 requests per minute on a free domain, a project with 10,000 tasks, paged at 100 per request, uses about 100 calls for one full read.
A second read in the same minute would exceed your quota, so you may need to wait for the Retry-After period before refreshing that data.
Move to a paid domain at 1,500 and you get roughly ten times that room.
Tightest of all is the Search API at 60 per minute. A workflow that searches once per task will stall after one minute's worth of tasks and need backoff on the 429 responses.

You won't find a per-call price in the documentation. Access appears to come with the plan, so the cost is the seat price. [G2's Asana pricing page](htt

access.title: Premium vs Business Account and API Access
access.snippet:
If you pay for any plan, you have access to the full API, including 1500 request/minute and the “search” endpoint.
Only free accounts are limited to 150 calls/minute, and they can’t access the “search tasks” endpoint.
[@Thiago4](https://forum.asana.com/u/thiago4) , just to clarify, though, the API follows the same feature availability as the Asana web app; so for example, switching from Business to Premium you’ll lose a bunch of end-user features and you’ll also lose those same capabilities in the API.

I’m not positive, but I’d guess since it’s just a number it represents org-wide number of projects, not limited by the requestor’s access rights. But one would need to confirm with [support@asana.com](mailto:support@asana.com) to be sure (or do a simple test–couldn’t you just advanced search for a person as a collaborator (member) of a project then in the results see the number in the Projects tab.

access.title: Rate limits
access.snippet:
Our standard rate limiter imposes a quota on how many requests can be made in a given window of time. Limits are based on minute-long windows and differ depending on whether the domain is free or paid (see [pricing](https://asana.com/pricing) for available tiers).
| Domain type | Maximum requests per minute |
|---|---|
| Free | 150 |
| Paid | 1,500 |
Example request:
```
GET https://app.asana.com/api/1.0/users/me HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer <personal_access_token>
```

access.title: Authentication
access.snippet:
Service Account
Similar to PATs, [Service Accounts](https://help.asana.com/s/article/service-accounts) (SAs) are long-lived tokens that provide programmatic access to the API. Service Accounts are an [Enterprise tier](https://asana.com/enterprise) feature and can only be created by Asana super admins (see more about [admin roles at Asana](https://help.asana.com/s/article/admin-and-super-admin-roles-in-asana)).
Unlike PATs, SAs provide complete access to all data within your Asana account, including private user data. As such, SAs are ideal if your app needs to have org-wide authorization. Some common use cases include:
- Creating periodic data backups
- Automating programmatic management of your Asana account. For example:
- User management and access based on company's policies
- Administrative tasks like team member management
- Cleaning up inactive projects
- Standardizing the structure of objects in your domain (e.g., portfolios, projects, custom fields, etc.)
- Building integrations that require access to all Asana data
- Authenticating Asana API endpoints that require service accounts. For example:
- [Audit log](/reference/audit-log-api)
- [Organizational exports](/reference/organization-exports)
- [SCIM](/docs/scim)
Instructions for Asana super admins to generate Service Accounts:
1. Click the **Apps** tab from within the admin console
2. Click **Service Accounts**
3. Click the **Add Service Account** button

mcp.title: Integrating with Asana's MCP Server
mcp.snippet:
The Asana V2 MCP server is generally available and uses OAuth for authorization. You'll pre-register your MCP app in the [developer console](https://app.asana.com/0/my-apps), where you can create both standard API apps and MCP apps.
The same registration steps apply to Asana's Command MCP server. Each user needs a Command license. For client-specific setup, see [Using Asana's Command MCP Server](https://developers.asana.com/docs/using-asanas-command-mcp-server).
**Important:** Tokens issued for MCP apps only work with the MCP server. This separation follows [MCP security best practices](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/basic/security_best_practices)—if a token is compromised, the blast radius is contained. If you need to make standard Asana API requests, create a separate API app and obtain tokens through the standard OAuth or PAT flow.

1. Go to the [developer console](https://app.asana.com/0/my-apps) and sign in
2. Click "Create new app"
3. Enter your app name (e.g., "My MCP Client")
4. Select "MCP app" as the app type
5. Click "Create app"

1. In the left sidebar, click "Manage distribution"
2. Under "Distribution method," choose one of the following:
- **Specific workspaces:** Select individual workspaces where you want the MCP integration to be usable
- **Any workspace:** Allow the app to be used in any workspace
3. If you selected "Specific workspaces," add the workspace(s) where you want to test
4. Click "Save changes"

The MCP authorization flow follows the same process as [our existing OAuth authorization flow](https://developers.asana.com/docs/oauth#user-authorization-endpoint), with one key difference: the optional `resource` parameter.
When directing users to the authorization endpoint, you can include the `resource` parameter to specify the MCP server:
```
https://app.asana.com/-/oauth_authorize
?client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID
&redirect_uri=YOUR_REDIRECT_URL
&response_type=code
&resource=https://mcp.asana.com/v2
&state=RANDOM_STRING
&code_challenge={SHA256_CHALLENGE}
&code_challenge_method=S256
```
**Parameters:**
- `resource` (optional): Use `https://mcp.asana.com/v2` for the Asana MCP server, or `https://mcp.asana.com/v2/command/mcp` for the Command MCP server.
- `scope` (optional): Use `default` or omit this parameter—MCP apps don't require specific scopes

Use the token with MCP
Once you have an access token, configure your MCP client to use it with the server you want to connect to:
- **Asana MCP server:** `https://mcp.a

mcp.title: MCP Tools Reference
mcp.snippet:
The Asana V2 MCP server exposes a set of tools that allow AI assistants to read from and write to your Asana workspace. This page describes the tools, what they do, and when to use them. Availability and tool versions can vary by client and rollout. Use `tools/list` in your connected client to see which tools are available to your session.

**How to use this reference**
Tools are grouped into three categories:
- **Read tools** return data from your workspace without making any changes.
- **Write tools** create, modify, or delete data in your workspace.
- **Interactive tools** display task search results or let you review a task or project before creating it. Availability depends on whether the client supports interactive apps.
**Access and permissions:** MCP apps in Asana do not use permission scopes. When a user authorizes an MCP client, the token automatically requests full access to all available tools. Once authorized, a tool cannot access projects, tasks, or data that the authenticated user does not already have permission to view in Asana.

- **Tokens are workspace-scoped.** When you authorize an MCP session, you select a specific workspace. All tool calls in that session are scoped to that workspace. To work across multiple workspaces, you need separate sessions.

mcp.title: developers.asana.com/docs/using-asanas-mcp-server.md
mcp.snippet:
Asana offers a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that allows AI assistants and other applications to access the Asana Work Graph. This server provides a way to interact with your Asana workspace through various AI platforms and tools that support MCP.
With this server, you can:
1. Access Asana data from compatible AI applications
2. Create and manage tasks and projects through natural language
3. Generate reports and summaries based on Asana data
4. Analyze project data and get AI-powered insights
Example requests:
1. "Find all my incomplete tasks due this week"
2. "Create a new task in the Marketing project assigned to me"
3. "List all sections in the Product Launch project"
4. "Show me the status of the Q2 Planning project"
## Requirements
1. A compatible MCP client (Streamable HTTP is supported). [There is a partial list of existing clients here!](https://developers.asana.com/docs/mcp-clients)
2. The above MCP client app (or the Asana MCP app, for beta clients) must not be blocked in your workspace via Asana [app management](https://help.asana.com/s/article/app-management-and-integrations?language=en_US). If it is, you will be prompted to send a request for your admin to unblock the app for your domain when trying to authorize.
***
# Connecting to Asana's MCP Server
The Asana MCP V2 server is available at: `https://mcp.asana.com/v2/mcp`.
This server requires authentication with your Asana account. When connecting, you'll be prompted to authorize the application to access your Asana data.

For MCP-compatible clients:
1. Configure your client to connect to `https://mcp.asana.com/v2/mcp`
2. Ensure your client supports OAuth authentication and Streamable HTTP transport
3. Set up the connection according to your client's documentation. You may need to use a client ID and client secret generated by following our [integration guide](https://developers.asana.com/docs/integrating-with-asanas-mcp-server), if the client doesn't manage this for you.
4. Authenticate with your Asana account when prompted

mcp.title: Connecting Coding Clients to Asana's V2 server
mcp.snippet:
The V2 MCP server (`https://mcp.asana.com/v2/mcp`) requires OAuth 2.0 authentication with a registered client ID and client secret. Pre-registration provides better security and gives organizations control over which applications can access their Asana data through app management. This guide shows you how to connect different MCP clients to the V2 server.

When creating your Asana MCP app, set the OAuth redirect URL in the developer console based on which client you're using:
- **Claude Code**: `http://localhost:8080/callback`
- **Cursor**: `cursor://anysphere.cursor-mcp/oauth/callback`
- **VS Code**: Both`http://127.0.0.1:33418/`and `https://vscode.dev/redirect`
- **Most other clients** (Windsurf, Kiro, Codex): `http://localhost:3334/oauth/callback`

You can connect Claude Code to Asana's V2 MCP server natively thanks to its support for OAuth pre-registration.
###
1. Prerequisites
- Claude Code installed ([download](https://code.claude.com))
- An Asana MCP app created ([create one](https://app.asana.com/0/my-apps))
- Your Client ID and Client secret from the Asana developer console
###
2. Add Asana MCP server to Claude Code
Open your terminal and run:
```
claude mcp add --transport http \
--client-id YOUR_CLIENT_ID \
--client-secret \
--callback-port 8080 \
asana https://mcp.asana.com/v2/mcp
```
- Replace `YOUR_CLIENT_ID` with your actual Asana Client ID.
- **Wait for the prompt**: After you hit Enter, Claude Code will ask you to enter you OAuth Client Secret.
- Paste your secret there. It will be hidden as you type and stored securely in your local configuration.

V1 server deprecation
> The V1 Beta MCP server `https://mcp.asana.com/sse` is deprecated and will shut down on **05/11/2026**. [Learn more and get migration steps in this changelog post](https://forum.asana.com/t/new-v2-mcp-server-now-generally-available/1122647)
Some clients such as Replit or Jetbrains doesn't support V2 OAuth pre-registration yet, you can continue using V1 until the deprecation date.

mcp.title: Using Asana's Command MCP Server
mcp.snippet:
Asana's Command MCP server lets compatible AI clients work with Command Teamspaces, tickets, and releases. You can search, create, and update tickets, add comments, manage blocking dependencies, and read release status.

Connecting to Asana's Command MCP Server
**Server URL:** `https://mcp.asana.com/v2/command/mcp`
Each user signs in with their own Asana account and authorizes access. To see available tools and their parameters, use your client's `tools/list` request.
##
Create an Asana MCP app
1. Open the [developer console](https://app.asana.com/0/my-apps), select **Create new app**, and choose **MCP app** as the app type.
2. In **OAuth**, add the redirect URL required by your client. It must match exactly.
3. In **Manage distribution**, allow the workspace where the app will be used.
Use the app's **Client ID** and **Client secret** when configuring your client. See [Integrating with Asana's MCP Server](https://developers.asana.com/docs/integrating-with-asanas-mcp-server) for app registration details. Use the Command server URL above when connecting.

mcp.title: GitHub - roychri/mcp-server-asana
mcp.snippet:
[![npm version](https://camo.githubusercontent.com/0a89c29b50fa7df529197b32344d00dc74e3c5a1c62a0520f0f7055194559953/68747470733a2f2f62616467652e667572792e696f2f6a732f253430726f79636872692532466d63702d7365727665722d6173616e612e737667)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@roychri/mcp-server-asana)
This Model Context Protocol server implementation of Asana allows you to talk to Asana API from MCP Client such as Anthropic's Claude Desktop Application, and many more.
More details on MCP here:
- [https://www.anthropic.com/news/model-context-protocol](https://www.anthropic.com/news/model-context-protocol)
- [https://modelcontextprotocol.io/introduction](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/introduction)
- [https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol)

## Environment Variables
- `ASANA_ACCESS_TOKEN`: (Required) Your Asana access token
- `READ_ONLY_MODE`: (Optional) Set to 'true' to disable all write operations. In this mode:
- Tools that modify Asana data (create, update, delete) will be disabled
- The `create-task` prompt will be disabled
- Only read operations will be available This is useful for testing or when you want to ensure no changes can be made to your Asana workspace.
## Usage
In the AI tool of your choice (ex: Claude Desktop) ask something about asana tasks, projects, workspaces, and/or comments. Mentioning the word "asana" will increase the chance of having the LLM pick the right tool.
Example:
> How many unfinished asana tasks do we have in our Sprint 30 project?

### For Claude Desktop:
Add the following to your `claude_desktop_config.json`:
```
{
"mcpServers": {
"asana": {
"command": "npx",
"args": ["-y", "@roychri/mcp-server-asana"],
"env": {
"ASANA_ACCESS_TOKEN": "your-asana-access-token"
}
}
}
}
```
